clue.text: Little girl to clean dog?

parts.note: to mop is to clean a floor with a mop
a dog is a typical pet

explanation.surface: Asks whether a young girl is being sent to wash the family dog.
explanation.definitionFit: Moppet is an affectionate word for a small child, especially a little girl.

clue.text: Two females, old and unintelligent, set up position in field

indicators.note: set up in a down clue means the letters are raised, read from bottom to top

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for female, so two of them give FF
dim means slow-witted

explanation.surface: Two dim old women are placed somewhere on a playing field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' reverses FF O DIM. MID-OFF is a cricket fielding position on the off side near the bowler.
explanation.definitionFit: Mid-off is a named fielding place in cricket, so it is a position in the field.

clue.text: Chum in US prison who may correspond with a stranger?

definitions.text: who may correspond with a stranger

parts.note: pen, short for penitentiary, is American slang for prison
a chum is a friend

explanation.surface: A prisoner's mate in an American jail writes letters to someone they have never met.
explanation.walkthrough: The chum is placed in the prison in the picture, but the pieces simply follow each other.
explanation.definitionFit: A pen pal exchanges letters with someone, often abroad, whom they have never met.

clue.text: New competitor in event ran terrifically

indicators.note: in says the letters lie within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A newcomer in a race ran brilliantly.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who enters a contest is a participant, often a new one.

clue.text: Fashionable item of clothes with gold edge, potential moneymaker

indicators.note: the gold forms the edge, so its letters sit at the end of the garment's

parts.note: something in fashion is said to be 'in'
a vest is an undergarment or waistcoat
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: Seems to describe a trendy garment trimmed with gold that might earn money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'edge' says the gold goes at the end, as a trim would; or is the heraldic word for gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who puts capital into a venture hopes it will make a profit, so is a would-be earner.

clue.text: Rudest alien removed and made ineffective

indicators.note: removed, read as re-moved, says the letters are moved around again

explanation.surface: A rude extraterrestrial is taken away and rendered harmless.
explanation.definitionFit: To neutralise something is to cancel its effect, making it powerless.

clue.text: English archdeacon at home — good time for putting feet up?

parts.note: Ven, for Venerable, is the title of an archdeacon
being at home is being in

explanation.surface: An English churchman relaxing at home, enjoying a rest.
explanation.walkthrough: An archdeacon in the Church of England is styled 'the Venerable', shortened to Ven.
explanation.definitionFit: The evening, after work, is when people typically relax with their feet up.

clue.text: Traveller in marketplace upset over limited parking

indicators.note: over in a down clue puts the first part above the second
upset in a down clue means the word is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: a mart is a market
P is the cut-down form of parking

explanation.surface: A wanderer in a market is annoyed at how little parking there is.
explanation.definitionFit: A tramp is a homeless person who travels about on foot.

clue.text: Furthest little spot found in holiday?

indicators.note: found in says the speck sits inside the holiday word

parts.note: a holiday is a rest
a mote is a speck of dust

explanation.surface: A tiny mark discovered while on vacation.
explanation.definitionFit: Remotest is the superlative of remote, meaning most distant.

clue.text: Show public school journalist around

indicators.note: around tells us to turn the school and journalist back to front

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public (fee-paying) school
ED is short for editor, the standard crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter is being shown round a famous school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' turns the whole school-plus-journalist string back to front. In Britain a public school is a private fee-paying one.
explanation.definitionFit: To denote something is to indicate or signify it, i.e. show it.

clue.text: Evangelist fighting against atheism ultimately becomes half-hearted

parts.note: Luke is one of the four Gospel writers, the Evangelists
fighting is war

indicators.note: ultimately picks the final letter of the word atheism

explanation.surface: A preacher's campaign against unbelief ends up lacking conviction.
explanation.definitionFit: Lukewarm means tepid, and figuratively lacking enthusiasm or commitment.

clue.text: Meet the old man outside wild party being taken short!

indicators.note: outside says the old man's letters wrap around the shortened party

parts.note: 'the old man' is slang for one's father

indicators.note: being taken short means losing its last letter

parts.note: an orgy is a wild party

explanation.surface: Someone's dad is caught short outside a riotous party and must find somewhere to go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken short' doubles as a joke about urgently needing a toilet; in the parse it lops the party's last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Forgather is an old-fashioned verb meaning to assemble or come together.

clue.text: See 22
Contribution I pen, finally turning up on time

indicators.note: finally takes the closing letter of the word pen
turning tells us to read the word up backwards

explanation.surface: A writer sends in a piece, finally getting it delivered on time.
explanation.definitionFit: Input is what someone contributes, such as ideas or work, to a shared effort.

clue.text: Perhaps butterfly chasers soon get lost — I'm sent out

indicators.note: sent out suggests the letters are dispatched and scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone told to get lost promptly, as if being dismissed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent out' rearranges SOON GET LOST plus I'M. 'Perhaps' marks butterfly chasers as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Insect scientists include those who study butterflies, so butterfly collectors are an example of them.

clue.text: Plans for plays? A censor is disturbed

indicators.note: disturbed says the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A theatre censor is upset by proposed scripts.
explanation.definitionFit: A scenario is the outline of a play or film's plot.

clue.text: Fascinating group, including one ex-GI?

indicators.note: including says the group word holds the other pieces

parts.note: a ring is a group, such as a gang of criminals
I is the Roman numeral for one
a vet is short for veteran, an ex-serviceman such as a former GI

explanation.surface: An intriguing band with a former American soldier in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Riveting means holding attention completely, as if fastened in place.

clue.text: Get painless in bed somehow — that's essential

indicators.note: somehow says the letters must be worked into some other order

explanation.surface: Advice to make yourself comfortable in bed, calling it vital.
explanation.definitionFit: Something essential cannot be done without, which is exactly what indispensable means.

clue.text: Designer of spreadsheet for pig farmer?

indicators.note: for here means belonging to, so the pig farmer's piece comes first

parts.note: a pig farmer's concern is the sty where pigs live
a spreadsheet is a list of data

explanation.surface: Asks who would design a spreadsheet for a pig farmer.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whimsically, a sty's list would be a pig farmer's spreadsheet.
explanation.definitionFit: A stylist designs hairstyles or clothes, so is a kind of designer.

clue.text: Head may have this message prohibiting money announced

parts.note: a ban is an order forbidding something

indicators.note: announced says the word is spoken, giving its sound

parts.note: dough is slang for money

explanation.surface: A headteacher might issue a notice banning cash.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandeau is a narrow headband worn around the hair.

clue.text: Bird awfully cagy needing to miss a trap

indicators.note: awfully suggests the remaining letters are badly mangled
needing to miss says the letter a is dropped from the word before

parts.note: a net is a trap

explanation.surface: A wary bird has to avoid a snare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing to miss' removes A from CAGY; 'awfully' rearranges CGY to CYG.
explanation.definitionFit: A cygnet is a young swan, so it is a bird.

clue.text: Middle of field has thin tree

indicators.note: Middle of takes the central letter of the five-letter word field

parts.note: thin and bony both describe a skinny build

explanation.surface: A spindly tree stands in the centre of a field.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebony is a tropical hardwood tree prized for its dark timber.

clue.text: Dramatist getting theatrical award meeting film producer with big mug

parts.note: an Oscar is an Academy Award, here loosely for the dramatic arts
Hammer Films is the British studio famous for horror movies
a stein is a large beer mug

explanation.surface: A playwright wins a prize and meets a studio boss holding a big beer mug.
explanation.walkthrough: Hammer is the British film company behind many classic horror films.
explanation.definitionFit: Oscar Hammerstein II wrote the books and lyrics for Broadway musicals such as Oklahoma!.

clue.text: Celebrity going round garden, ending in rockery, sitting down

indicators.note: going round says the celebrity's letters surround the garden

parts.note: a celebrity is a star
Eden is the biblical garden

indicators.note: ending in takes the last letter of rockery

explanation.surface: A famous person strolls round a garden and ends up sitting in the rockery.
explanation.definitionFit: A sedentary job or lifestyle involves much sitting, so the word describes being seated.

clue.text: Well-disposed, like a bank?

definitions.meaning: favourably minded, as in being minded to agree
a river bank or hillside slopes, so is at an angle

explanation.surface: Wonders whether a friendly attitude resembles a bank's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' suggests money, but here it is a slope.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both favourably disposed and sloping, as a bank of earth does.

clue.text: Military unit in district given new leader

indicators.note: given new leader says the first letter of the district word is replaced

parts.note: a region is a district or area

explanation.surface: An army unit stationed in an area gets a new commander.
explanation.walkthrough: The new first letter is L, replacing the R.
explanation.definitionFit: A legion was a Roman army division and is still used for a large military force.

clue.text: Spinning round, I get angry, mad, losing energy

indicators.note: mad suggests the remaining letters are crazily jumbled
losing says that letter is dropped from the words before them

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone whirling about in a rage until they run out of steam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' drops E (energy) from I GET ANGRY, leaving IGTANGRY, which 'mad' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: To gyrate is to revolve or whirl, so gyrating means turning in circles.

clue.text: Group on newspaper accounting for daily event

indicators.note: on places the group after the newspaper in this across answer

parts.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper
a set is a group of things

explanation.surface: A team at a newspaper reports on something that happens every day.
explanation.walkthrough: THE SUN is a British tabloid daily newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: The sun goes down every evening, so its setting is a recurring daily occurrence.
